actual_scope_finding.evidence: The opening asserts finite point-blowup resolution on 'an arbitrary regular surface', assuming only finite normalization of each curve component. The cited theorem instead states: 'Let S be a regular surface: a Noetherian scheme of pure dimension two all of whose local rings are regular.' The scoped SNC definition allows locally Noetherian surfaces, so Noetherianity is not implicit in that terminology. Counterexample: take S to be a countably infinite disjoint union of affine planes over Q and Z the disjoint union of cusps y^2=x^3, one in each plane. S is a locally Noetherian regular surface of pure dimension two, Z is a reduced curve, and every component has finite normalization. Finitely many blowups at individual closed points affect only finitely many connected components, leaving infinitely many singular cusps; consequently the final support cannot be SNC. The opening needs the theorem's Noetherian hypothesis.
